A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UniSim study. The complete main text and Appendices A–F are available, and their text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original molecular simulation evaluations in Tables 1–3, alanine-dipeptide experiments, and appendix ablation and efficiency results.

after.justification: v3 retains the original molecular simulation evaluations, alanine-dipeptide experiments, and appendix ablation and efficiency results.

M1.justification: The pretraining components, stochastic-interpolant model, force-guidance kernel and inference refinement procedure are unchanged. The revised ATLAS timestep is an experimental setting, not a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same pretraining datasets and evaluate small molecules, PepMD peptides, ATLAS proteins and alanine-dipeptide. The ATLAS timing revisions concern the retained experiment's settings rather than added dataset or domain coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches: Table 1 includes FBM, Timewarp, ITO and SD; Table 3 includes FBM, ITO and SD. The UniSim/g comparisons and OpenMM efficiency comparison are also retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D, Table 7 rescales ATLAS frame spacing from 10 ps to 100 ps, simulation time per trajectory from 10 ns to 100 ns, and coarsened timestep from 100 ps to 1 ns. These tenfold revisions substantially change the documented physical sampling and prediction timescales for the protein experiments. They establish a reported protocol revision, but do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The force-guidance comparisons, alanine-dipeptide case study, SDE-step and guidance-strength sensitivity analysis, atomic-embedding ablation, and refinement-efficiency analysis are all retained with the same evidence.

E5.justification: Mean/std reporting across test molecules is unchanged. Table 8 already reports averaging three independent runs per peptide in v1, and v3 retains that practice and the statistical displays in Figure 8.

E6.justification: The outcome values and findings in Tables 1–3 and 8–9, Figures 3–8, and the accompanying prose match. Table 7 changes experimental settings rather than outcomes; the unchanged ATLAS results do not establish a performance improvement under comparable settings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives and derivations are unchanged, including Proposition 3.1 and its proof in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified cross-domain simulation, atomic pretraining, force-guided adaptation and competitive empirical performance.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of force guidance and transferability, and the same limitations concerning accumulated errors, unreliable protein conformations and short evaluation trajectories.

D1.justification: The three revised ATLAS timing entries in Table 7 change reproducibility information. Other implementation details, hyperparameters, processing instructions, code-access information and computing infrastructure in Appendices A–F remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning match, including the relationships to FBM, DPA-2 and earlier molecular pretraining and time-coarsened dynamics methods.

P1.justification: Page 1 replaces the Beijing Key Laboratory affiliation with the Engineering Research Center of Next-Generation Intelligent Search and Recommendation, MOE, and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: Figures 1–8, table structures, captions and page organization are retained. The revised Table 7 entries do not change its display design.

improvement.justification: The consequential revision is the tenfold change to ATLAS timing in Table 7, while Table 3 results and Figure 5 remain identical. The PDFs do not explain whether this corrects earlier reporting or reflects changed experiments, so an improvement in reproducibility or evidential support cannot be established. The remaining changes are administrative and do not resolve that uncertainty.
